title: Plymouth Valiant Engines by Year (1960–1976)
description: Every factory engine in the Plymouth Valiant by year, 1960–1976: the 170 and 225 slant sixes it introduced, the 198, and the 273 and 318 V8s.
intro: The Valiant was Plymouth's compact from 1960 to 1976 and the car that introduced Chrysler's slant six. It was sold as a separate Valiant brand in 1960 and as a Plymouth from 1961; the Duster, its coupe version, has its own page.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Valiants used the 170 and, from 1961, the 225 slant six. The 273, Chrysler's first small-block V8, arrived in 1964, with a four-barrel Commando version from 1965.
The 1967 redesign kept the slant sixes and small blocks; the 318 joined in 1968 and the 198 six replaced the 170 in 1970. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
